newsitem.title: UK: ABF shares up as analysts applaud Irish sale.
newsitem.headline: ABF shares up as analysts applaud Irish sale.

text.p: Shares in Associated British Foods Plc climbed on Friday, after the company announced it was selling its Irish food retailing and related businesses to Tesco Plc for 630 million stg.
The shares were 11p higher at 522-1/2 by 1244 GMT. Tesco was four pence firmer at 343.

"The market was a bit worried about the prospects for those businesses with the UK food retailers moving into Ireland anyway, so it's a problem dealt with in that sense," said Michael Bourke, analyst at Panmure Gordon.

"The price is fairly good. There will be a small dilution to ABF's earnings but they've got a good offer and there were obviously risks of price wars and so on in Ireland, so they were maybe better to leave it to Tesco."
ABF said it would receive a 10 million stg dividend from the businesses ahead of the sale, on top of the price paid by Tesco.
"The deal looks good, it's a reasonable price and it means ABF are getting out of a market that is becoming increasingly competitive," another analyst said.
Bourke said ABF was unlikely to rush into any acquisitions.

"They had a pretty sizeable cash pile before, and have had for some time," he said. "So I don't think they've sold these businesses so they can buy something. This decision has been taken on its own merits."
But the company was likely to examine a few possible acquisition opportunities this year, Bourke said.

"I am sceptical of these rumours that they would look at something like Hillsdown," he said. But he added that the company might be interested in buying some speciality chemicals businesses put up for sale by Unilever Plc. It might also consider buying parts of the Polish sugar industry, which is being privatised this year.

"But they will be careful in spending the money," he said. "They have had this cash pile for a decade or more and have let a lot of things pass them by because they thought they were too expensive or didn't fit or whatever."
